corpus: original model suggestion text with verified acceptance in earlier sessions
finding: No useful primary personal advantage is established. Useful base and uniform advantage remains unresolved under both interval methods; pooled and donor advantage is excluded under both. The primary base writer interval narrowly favors personal adaptation at zero without establishing useful advantage or surviving crossed resampling at zero. All other primary intervals include zero. Adapted-minus-base donor, pooled and uniform useful advantages are excluded under writer resampling but remain unresolved under crossed resampling; all residual intervals include zero. Raw sums exclude useful advantage against every rival under both methods. Raw base favors personal adaptation at zero only under writer resampling; raw pooled and donor intervals include zero, and raw sums are worse than uniform under both methods. No parity follows.
limits: Previously selected model prose reflects suggestion supply and prior choices, not human-authored text or necessarily final retained wording. Sparse histories, shared or changed human support, fixed donor/global training and exposed prompts bound the recipe. No independent human confirmation, seed/corpus ranking, population limit, private-goal inference or whole-matrix verdict. Earlier failed/unknown attempts remain separate; no new retry.
